transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-13 10:30 UTC | Duration: 43m
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Ivy (Redwood CSM) — Rajesh, Maya, Liam, Nora, Devon (Finova)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough): staging parity focus; access gaps (KMS, service account), plan to run 24h shadow bench once creds are in; exchange security docs and pricing sketch; possible follow-up latency deep dive.

00:00 Samira Lopez: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday morning, appreciate it. quick agenda — staging parity checks, access updates, bench plan, and open Qs.
00:18 Rajesh Iyer: thanks, yeah this week we mostly hit the network weirdness, some of the calls to the gateway timeout at tail. also saw differing token counts between hosted and our staging runs.
00:35 Marcus Chen: okay, that matches what we suspected — a routing MTU issue might be dropping larger batches, also need to confirm K-V cache persistence on your side, sometimes the K-V cache is... um, not persisted across hot restarts in our staging image if the volume mount is missing.
00:52 Maya Torres: yep we spun up the staging nodes with ephemeral storage initially, that'll explain cache volatility. we're adding a PVC today.
01:05 Samira Lopez: good, PVC will fix the KV cache persistence. quick clarification — are you running the staging stack through the VPN to the Redwood gateway or direct egress to the hosted endpoints?
01:20 Devon Kim: current plan is egress through our corporate NAT to hosted Redwood endpoints in us-east. we tried a V-P-C peering but it introduced asymmetrical routes so we backed off.
01:36 Marcus Chen: asym routes can cause increased latency and retransmits. for the bench we recommend either a direct egress path with stable NAT or setting up the dedicated peering but with correct route tables.
01:52 Liam O'Neill: long-term we want a private deployment but for the pilot we want to validate performance on Hosted vs Dedicated profiles. what's a realistic delta between hosted and dedicated?
02:10 Marcus Chen: ballpark — dedicated with reserved GPUs and kernel tuning usually gives 10–40% better p50 depending on model and quant profile. p99 improvements depend on batching and prefix cache effectiveness; if you can persist K-V cache and run steady traffic we expect smaller tail variance.
02:30 Nora Park: question on encryption — we need to ensure customer-managed keys for any model artifacts or logs. do you support KMS wrap/un-wrap?
02:42 Samira Lopez: yes we support KMS integrations, we can either integrate with your cloud KMS or use Redwood-managed with BYOK. for Private deployments it's customer-managed by default. we'll include a KMS diagram in the security pack.
02:58 Rajesh Iyer: were there any anomalies in tokenization that might explain token count differences? the same prompt on hosted produced 2 tokens less on average.
03:12 Marcus Chen: sometimes tokenization differs due to tokenizer version or pre-tokenization normalization; we shipped a tokenizer shim in the last model bundle — I'll confirm exact version. could also be trailing whitespace or encoding differences.
03:28 Rajesh Iyer: ok please confirm.
03:33 Samira Lopez: quick access status? Maya/Maya?
03:36 Maya Torres: we created the redwood-poc-sa but haven't granted KMS wrap perms yet — waiting on the security team's scoping. also network team flagged outbound connection timeouts to the region-gateway at 10:15 last night (we'll attach logs).
03:52 Marcus Chen: those timeouts line up with MTU fragmentation — do you have jumbo frames turned on anywhere?
04:01 Devon Kim: no jumbo frames intentionally, but we do have a couple of load balancers with 1500 over tunnel.
04:10 Marcus Chen: if the path MTU is lower somewhere in tunnel, large batched messages could be dropped; for immediate mitigation reduce max batch size in the runner to avoid fragmentation.
04:25 Samira Lopez: action item — Marcus will give a recommended max batch size for interim runs. Marcus?
04:29 Marcus Chen: yep I'll run an instrumented bench to show safe batch sizes per sequence length, send that by end of day tomorrow.
04:40 Rajesh Iyer: and on the KV cache behavior — we need to know how cache warming changes p50/p99; can we instrument that in the shadow bench?
04:53 Marcus Chen: absolutely, bench will include cold-warm runs. we'll do ramp up, steady state, and then a simulated restart to validate cache warmup times.
05:05 Nora Park: about observability — do you expose token-level traces or only aggregates? we need detail to root cause accuracy regressions.
05:18 Marcus Chen: token-level traces are captured in the trial retention, we can hook into span-level traces and give you sample payloads; for pilot we'll enable extended retention for your project.
05:30 Rajesh Iyer: great. also curious on costing — if we run the 24hr shadow bench, will that cost be billed in the pilot? we need to model.
05:41 Samira Lopez: we typically treat bench runs as billable under the pilot committed usage; but we'll provide a pricing sketch and example token profiles so you can model it. small bench adjustments during troubleshooting we usually absorb.
05:55 Liam O'Neill: fine. one more — compliance: audit logs, SSO and RBAC. can we lock down who can retrieve logs?
06:07 Samira Lopez: yes RBAC controls are per project; SSO via SAML is supported; we'll include a short how-to to limit log visibility and set up audit pipelines.
06:20 Maya Torres: perfect, send docs.
06:24 Samira Lopez: we'll send SOC2 extract and the KMS diagram and RBAC guide.
06:29 Rajesh Iyer: cool. walking through bench plan — Marcus you said you'll prepare the shadow script. what's the expected traffic shape?
06:40 Marcus Chen: we'll mirror a 10 TPS steady-state with 80% short sequences (<=128 tokens) and 20% long tails (~1024 token prompts) to stress KV cache and batching differences. We'll run a cold-start phase, warmup, steady 24 hours, and then a deliberate failover to simulate restarts.
07:00 Dev: sounds good. when do you need creds?
07:03 Maya Torres: once we grant KMS wrap key and attach SA perms we'll message you. aiming EOD 4/15.
07:12 Samira Lopez: perfect. Marcus will only run after creds are validated.
07:16 Marcus Chen: noted. also, small gotcha — your staging image earlier used an older glibc which caused a misaligned vector instruction on the quant kernels; we caught an AVX fallback that increased latency. please ensure runtime libs match our recommended stack.
07:36 Devon Kim: thanks we'll align container base image and send a reproducible image hash.
07:44 Rajesh Iyer: any blockers on our side for dedicated pilot profiling?
07:50 Marcus Chen: only the service account and KMS perms plus stable routing; once we have those the 24h bench should give a clear delta between hosted vs your dedicated-like config.
07:59 Samira Lopez: ok recap — deliverables: Samira sends security pack + pricing sketch (4/16), Maya/Devon provision SA + KMS (4/15), Marcus prepares and runs bench once creds are in (target 4/20) and gives recommended interim batch sizes, Finova will send network traceroutes and container image hash. if bench shows >15% tail regression we'll schedule a deep latency triage 4/22.
08:25 Nora Park: quick nit — please include sample failure mode for KV eviction in the docs; we had a previous outage caused by eviction storms.
08:35 Marcus Chen: will do, include eviction thresholds and recommended memory targets per instance.
08:42 Rajesh Iyer: one last ask — can Redwood capture a baseline run on hosted for us to compare?
08:48 Samira Lopez: yes we can run a hosted baseline concurrently and provide the artifact and diff sheet.
08:55 Liam O'Neill: awesome. thanks everyone — that's it from Finova side.
09:00 Samira Lopez: thanks team, we'll follow up with the pack and schedule.

Meeting end: 11:13 UTC (timestamps in transcript are approximate to sections)

References shared: link: /redwood/pilot/finova/security-pack-v1.pdf (Samira will send), link: /redwood/pilot/finova/bench-script-v1.sh (Marcus to share after run).

Note on transcript: minor mis-recognitions present (VPC sometimes spelled V-P-C, KV cache as K-V cache), filler talk and cross talk preserved.
